04 / 10 Application architecture

One server. Two separate sockets.

TCP and UDP can use the same port number without sharing a socket.

Same number, different transport.The OS distinguishes TCP port 5000 from UDP port 5000. Our server opens a TCP listener and a separate UDP socket.

Share a link. Players install nothing.npm start opens a free Cloudflare tunnel: a public HTTPS link that works from any network. The browser leg always uses WebSocket/TCP; the TCP/UDP switch applies between gateway and game server.

client/game/net-shim.js · server/gateway.js · server/server.jsSOCKET COMMUNICATION
05 / 10 Simultaneous players & disconnections

Many players at once. A lost player never stops the race.

Simultaneous players

  • Each player has their own connection: a WebSocket, plus their own TCP and UDP sockets from the gateway to the server.
  • Node.js handles one event at a time, very fast (event loop): messages never mix and no locks are needed.
  • Rooms are separate: messages only reach players in the same room.
  • Same moment, same item box? The server decides: first claim wins, one hit per projectile, finish order = arrival order.

Disconnections

  • Tab closed or crash: the connection closes, and the server removes the player.
  • Cable pulled or PC frozen: no heartbeat for 3 s, and the server removes the player.
  • The others see “PLAYER LEFT”; the kart disappears and the race continues.
  • The bot driver or room creator role passes to the next player.
  • Broken messages are ignored and every handler runs in try/catch, so the server never crashes.

06 / 10 TCP implementation

Reliable events keep the race consistent.

TCP

Ordered byte stream · retransmission of lost data

  • Login, room membership and character selection.
  • Race grid, readiness, countdown and results.
  • Lap reports, item use and hit claims.

A missing position can be replaced. A missing “race finished” event changes the outcome.

On the wire · newline-delimited JSON
{"t":"login","name":"Ana"}\n
{"t":"loaded"}\n
{"t":"finish","kart":2}\n

Implementation details

Buffer incoming bytes, split at \n, then parse JSON. One socket read may contain part of a message or several messages.

setNoDelay(true) disables Nagle batching for small messages. Loss recovery can still delay newer data.

server/gateway.js · server/server.js · RFC 9293RELIABILITY & ORDERING
07 / 10 UDP implementation

For movement, newer state matters.

UDP

Independent datagrams · no automatic retry or ordering

Send position snapshots at a target of about 30 updates/s: coordinates, heading, speed, track progress and flags.

{ "t":"s", "id":1, "raceId":7,
  "seq":104, "k":[[2,12,0,8,1.2,30,0.5,1,0]] }

Illustrative payload · one client includes bot positions too.

In our browser version, players reach the host over WebSocket (TCP); this UDP path runs between our gateway and the game server.

Latest-state rule
101→102 ×→103

Accept 103. Keep moving.

Compare sequence numbers per sender. Ignore duplicate or older updates; reject a different race ID.

Predict between updates

Estimate remote movement using heading and speed, then smooth toward new snapshots.

This can hide short gaps. Sustained loss still causes visible errors.
